_comment: Named, seeded scenario definitions (design-specification.md section 3.5 Scenario). Data-driven on purpose: adding or adjusting a scenario should not require a Go code change. reader_id/door_id/direction are fixed because this slice simulates exactly one controlled door (REQ-TOPO-004); kind selects which of the three small execution strategies internal/simulator/scenarios.go uses.

normal-day.description: Several authorized users generate normal accesses spread over model time (REQ-SIM-001/002).

authorized-passage.description: One authorized user, full successful-passage sequence (REQ-FUNC-004, REQ-SIM-005/006).

unauthorized-access.description: A user/card without permission on this door attempts entry (REQ-AUTH, REQ-SIM-004).

after-hours-access.description: A normally-authorized user accesses at an unusual model time; authorization stays ALLOW, anomaly detection should classify it ANOMALOUS.

rapid-repeat-access.description: The same person presents repeatedly over a short model-time interval, for anomaly/data-quality evaluation.

burst-access.description: Configurable number/rate of presentations by one person, for latency/stress evaluation. count/interval_ms may be overridden per run.

decision-service-failure.description: A single authorized presentation, meant to be issued while the Decision Service is killed/restarted around this call (see scripts/run-local.sh demo-decision-failure and docs/scenarios.md).

actuator-or-buildsim-failure.description: A single authorized presentation, meant to be issued while the Door Actuator or BuildSim is stopped around this call (see scripts/run-local.sh demo-actuator-failure and docs/scenarios.md).
